# Results — Study 961 (Which Gold) on the real daily tape

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). Five US physically-backed gold
trusts — **GLD, IAU, GLDM, SGOL, BAR** — measured against each other and against the
equal-weight cohort mean on daily adjusted closes (`yfinance`, `auto_adjust=True`). None of
the five has ever paid a distribution (they sell bullion to pay the sponsor fee), so for
them the **adjusted close is the price close** and the total-return / price-only labels
coincide; **BIL** is genuine total return and appears only in the excess-of-cash race.
Common window 2018-06-26 → 2026-06-30 (GLDM's inception gates it). As-of **2026-06-30** —
the partial current month is dropped so the monthly estimator never eats a stub.*

## Data stamp

| Legs | Window | n days | n months | Fingerprint |
|---|---|---|--:|---|
| GLD, IAU, GLDM, SGOL, BAR | 2018-06-26 → 2026-06-30 | 2,013 | 96 | Fingerprint `9af52c692ea9` |

Cash leg: BIL (total return). Liquidity leg: daily close × volume per wrapper, cached as
`dvol_<TICKER>_1d.parquet`.

## The non-tape inputs, named

| Input | Value | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Published sponsor fees (bp/yr) | GLD 40.00, IAU 25.00, GLDM 10.00, SGOL 17.00, BAR 17.49 | **ASSUMPTION** — *today's* fee sheet, not a tape. Carries hindsight: on the first day of the window GLDM charged 18 bp and was **not** the cheapest of the five. |
| In-window fee change | GLDM 18 → 10 bp effective 2020-10-01 | **ASSUMPTION** — an announcement date, invisible on a price tape. It is also the **only** change this study records; the record is not independently exhaustive, and an unrecorded cut at another wrapper would move the blended sheet. |
| Choice of the headline pair | GLDM vs GLD | **SELECTION** off that sheet. The *number* is pure tape; which two wrappers get differenced is not. It is the widest published gap, so it is also the pair with the most to find. |
| Round-trip execution differential | 0 → 30 bp | **ASSUMPTION**, swept. No free tape carries quoted spreads. |
| Borrow on the short leg | 0 → 100 bp/yr | **ASSUMPTION**, swept. |
| Capital-gains rate / embedded gain | 15 / 20 / 23.8%, ×0.2 → ×3.0 | **ASSUMPTION**, swept. |

Every headline number below — the pairwise spreads, the era cut, the ownership race — is
**pure tape** and uses none of these. The fee sheet enters only the rank and pass-through
tests, which are reported against today's sheet, the time-blended sheet, and rank order
alone.

**Survivorship.** These are five wrappers that still exist in 2026. Closed bullion vehicles
are absent by construction, which flatters the *level* of the cohort mean; it cannot
manufacture the cross-sectional fee ordering, which is the claim under test.

## Measurement floor

Averaged over all ten pairs, a wrapper-minus-wrapper difference has a standard deviation of
**7.43 bp/day** and **9.2 bp/month**. Over 96 non-overlapping months that puts the smallest
gap this tape could separate from zero at |*t*| = 2 at **22.5 bp/yr**. The published fee
spread across the cohort is 30 bp. The tape is therefore able to resolve the *coarse*
ranking and nothing finer — a fact the pair table below makes explicit.

## Which *t* this study quotes, and why it is the smaller one

The wrapper-versus-wrapper residual **mean-reverts** — acf1 = **−0.46 daily** and still
**−0.42 monthly**. That inverts the usual reason for a Newey-West *t*: the HAC long-run
variance sits *below* the iid one, so the HAC *t* is roughly **twice** the naive one and it
keeps climbing with the bandwidth:

| Bandwidth | naive (iid) | HAC 1 | HAC 2 | HAC 3 | HAC 4 | HAC 6 | HAC 8 | HAC 12 |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| *t* on GLDM − GLD (monthly) | **+3.18** | +4.22 | +5.47 | +6.32 | +6.48 | +7.56 | +8.36 | +9.43 |

A *t* that grows with a knob is a choice, not evidence. **Every headline *t* below is
therefore the naive iid one**, with the HAC value in brackets for continuity, and the
interval the verdict has to survive is the **iid** bootstrap, not the block bootstrap
(which inherits the same mean reversion and prints narrower).

## Realised tracking difference vs the equal-weight cohort mean

| Wrapper | Fee (bp/yr) | Monthly TD (bp/yr) | *t* (naive) | [HAC] | Months up | Daily TD | Endpoint TD |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **GLD** | 40.00 | **−16.75** | **−3.02** | [−6.95] | 32/96 | −17.20 | −17.14 |
| IAU | 25.00 | −2.24 | −0.31 | [−0.62] | 47/96 | −1.44 | −1.43 |
| **GLDM** | 10.00 | **+9.43** | +1.80 | [+3.45] | 59/96 | +9.17 | +9.13 |
| SGOL | 17.00 | +5.41 | +0.56 | [+1.04] | 49/96 | +4.30 | +4.29 |
| BAR | 17.49 | +4.15 | +0.54 | [+1.02] | 51/96 | +5.17 | +5.15 |

The three estimators agree to within ~1 bp on every wrapper, which is what a clean,
same-strike cohort should look like. On the honest *t*, **one** wrapper separates from the
cohort mean on its own: GLD, the priciest, at −3.02. GLDM's +9.43 is the right sign and the
right size but only *t* = +1.80 — a 9 bp effect against a 22.5 bp floor is not a
one-wrapper result, which is exactly why the study leans on the widest *pair* and on the
*joint* ranking rather than on any single wrapper's *t*.

**Fee-rank test.** Spearman(fee, tracking difference) = **−1.0000** on today's sheet and on
the time-blended sheet alike: the realised ordering is the exact reverse of the fee
ordering, with no inversions. The exact permutation *p* is **0.0167** — and that is the
**hard floor** with five funds (2/120 permutations), so a perfect match cannot buy a
smaller *p*. Cross-sectional pass-through of fee into tracking difference: slope **−0.894**
(R² 0.992) on today's sheet, **−0.943** (R² 0.999) on the time-blended sheet.

## The headline pair — GLDM (10 bp) minus GLD (40 bp)

The *measurement* uses no fee number at all. **Which** two wrappers get differenced does:
the pair is read off today's sheet, and it is the widest gap on it.

| Estimator | Spread (bp/yr) | *t* (naive) | [HAC] | Detail |
|---|--:|--:|--:|---|
| **Monthly, non-overlapping** | **+26.17** | **+3.18** | [+6.32] | 65/96 months up, **9/9 calendar years up**, sd 6.7 bp/month, acf1 −0.42 |
| Daily | +26.36 | +0.78 | [+2.19] | sd 5.98 bp/day, acf1 **−0.462** — powerless at this frequency |
| Endpoint | +26.28 | — | — | two anchors only |

| Bootstrap (5,000 draws) | 95% CI (bp/yr) | Share of resamples < 0 |
|---|---|--:|
| **iid — the conservative one** | **[+9.54, +41.88]** | 0.06% |
| Moving block, 3 months | [+17.09, +35.28] | 0.00% |

Read the wide interval: the tape says the gap is somewhere between **10 and 42 bp/yr**, not
that it is 26. What it does not say is zero — under either resampling scheme, and with the
sign holding in **every one of the nine calendar years** in the window (2018 and 2026 are
part-years).

The daily estimator is the honest picture of how little a day carries: naive *t* = +0.78 on
a 26 bp/yr effect against 6 bp/day of premium noise. Its HAC *t* of +2.19 is not a rescue —
it is the mean reversion shrinking the long-run variance. Monthly aggregation is the right
construction because the observations are non-overlapping and most of the transient premium
is gone; it is **not** a more conservative one, and the study does not claim it is.

**The 4 bp that do not show up.** The realised gap is 26.2 bp against a 30 bp current-sheet
gap. Time-blending GLDM's 18 bp launch fee gives an expected 27.7 bp — so roughly half the
shortfall is fee history and the rest sits well inside the iid bootstrap's ±16 bp
half-width. The tape
hands back the fee; it does not pin it to the basis point.

## All ten pairs — the joint pattern

| Pair | Fee gap (bp) | Realised (bp/yr) | *t* (naive) | [HAC] | Months up |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| GLD–GLDM | −30.00 | −26.17 | **−3.18** | [−6.32] | 31/96 |
| GLD–SGOL | −23.00 | −22.16 | −1.91 | [−3.78] | 35/96 |
| GLD–BAR | −22.51 | −20.89 | −1.91 | [−3.87] | 34/96 |
| GLD–IAU | −15.00 | −14.51 | −1.47 | [−3.37] | 40/96 |
| IAU–GLDM | −15.00 | −11.66 | −1.28 | [−2.58] | 45/96 |
| IAU–SGOL | −8.00 | −7.65 | −0.49 | [−0.94] | 49/96 |
| IAU–BAR | −7.51 | −6.38 | −0.63 | [−1.17] | 42/96 |
| GLDM–SGOL | +7.00 | +4.02 | +0.34 | [+0.63] | 50/96 |
| GLDM–BAR | +7.49 | +5.28 | +0.49 | [+0.97] | 50/96 |
| SGOL–BAR | +0.49 | +1.26 | +0.08 | [+0.16] | 46/96 |

Every one of the ten realised spreads has the **sign the fee sheet predicts** and lands
within ~4 bp of the fee gap — and that joint pattern, not any individual *t*, is the
cross-sectional evidence (ten of ten correct signs; the rank test below scores it formally).
Taken one at a time on the honest *t*, only **one** pair clears |*t*| = 2: the widest one.
GLD–SGOL and GLD–BAR sit at 1.9 — right size, right sign, not significant alone — and the
four single-digit gaps are invisible against the 22.5 bp floor, exactly as the floor says
they must be. The ladder is legible at the top, suggestive in the middle, and unreadable at
the rungs.

## Robustness — two eras (split 2022-01-01)

| Era | n months | GLDM − GLD (bp/yr) | *t* (naive) | [HAC] | Months up |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 2018-07 → 2021-12 | 42 | **+20.98** | +1.43 | [+2.87] | 23/42 |
| 2022-01 → 2026-06 | 54 | **+30.21** | **+3.28** | [+6.62] | 42/54 |

Positive in **both** halves; significant on the honest *t* in the **late** one only. Said
plainly: the early era is the right sign and the right size but **not** significant on its
own — 42 months of a ~21 bp effect against a 22.5 bp detection floor cannot be, arithmetically.
The era cut therefore buys sign-stability, not two independent confirmations. The early era's
smaller number is what GLDM's 18 bp launch fee (cut to 10 bp on 2020-10-01) implies; the late
era, entirely under today's sheet, prints +30.21 against a 30.00 bp fee gap.

**Fee-stable sub-window** (2021-01-01 →, today's sheet holds for all five, 65 months):
GLDM − GLD = **+26.66 bp/yr**, *t* = **+2.69** naive [HAC +5.24], 47/65 months up; Spearman
still **−1.0000** (*p* = 0.0167). This is the cut that matters most, because it is the one
window in which no fee assumption is doing any work — and it clears |*t*| = 2 on its own.

## What the gap is worth to a buy-and-hold holder

At the realised +26.17 bp/yr, holding the priciest wrapper instead of the cheapest costs, as
a share of terminal wealth on an untouched bullion sleeve:

| Horizon | Shortfall | Per $100,000 |
|---|--:|--:|
| 1 yr | 0.262% | $262 |
| 5 yr | 1.302% | $1,302 |
| **10 yr** | **2.587%** | **$2,587** |
| 20 yr | 5.107% | $5,107 |

## Ownership race, excess-of-cash (one execution lag on the only rule that trades)

| Arm | Excess Sharpe | CAGR | Vol |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| Own cheapest (GLDM) | 0.7799 | +15.476% | 17.05% |
| Own priciest (GLD) | 0.7613 | +15.172% | 17.14% |
| Chase last year's tracking winner | 0.7762 | +15.427% | 17.09% |

The cash leg is **BIL**, a *proxy* for the risk-free rate rather than the rate itself: it is
an ETF and charges its own fee. It is subtracted from **all three** arms, so it lowers every
excess Sharpe by the same amount and cancels out of the gap between them.

Sharpe gap cheapest − priciest: **+0.0187**. **No *t* is quoted on that gap** — the study
runs no inference on a Sharpe difference. The *t* on the underlying daily return difference
is +0.74 naive [HAC +2.06], i.e. the daily view is powerless in both directions; the
monthly estimator above is the evidence, and the race is here to show what 26 bp/yr looks
like inside a performance table (two hundredths of a Sharpe point on a 17%-vol asset —
real, and invisible).

The chase rule — rank on the trailing 12 months of cohort-relative tracking difference
through the last session of the year, **fill at the next session's close so the new wrapper
first earns on the session after that**, 2 bp one-way × NAV per leg, 4 switches over the
window — **loses** to simply owning the cheapest (*t* on the difference = −0.14 naive
[HAC −0.41]). It loses even though it is handed the fee-cheapest wrapper for free in the
first half-year, before it has any signal. Chasing the tracking winner is not the trade;
buying the cheap wrapper is.

## The counterweights

**1. Liquidity (real tape, close × volume, last 12 months).** The cheapest wrapper is only
the right answer if you can buy it in size.

| Wrapper | Median daily $ volume | A $100m ticket = |
|---|--:|--:|
| GLD | $4,085m | 0.02 days of ADV |
| IAU | $654m | 0.15 days |
| **GLDM** | **$433m** | **0.23 days** |
| SGOL | $175m | 0.57 days |
| **BAR** | **$21m** | **4.80 days** |

GLDM absorbs an institutional ticket in a quarter of a session, so for the *headline* pair
the liquidity objection does not bite. It bites hard on the two thinnest wrappers: BAR needs
nearly a week of full participation to fill $100m, which is why "cheapest fee" and "best
wrapper" part company below the top of the table.

**2. A wider round-trip execution differential (ASSUMPTION, swept).**

| Round trip | Repaid in |
|---|--:|
| 1 bp | 14 days |
| 2 bp | 28 days |
| 5 bp | 70 days |
| 10 bp | 140 days |
| 30 bp | 418 days |

Even a punitive 30 bp round-trip penalty is repaid inside fourteen months of holding.

**3. Switching an appreciated taxable holding (ASSUMPTION, swept).** US bullion trusts are
taxed as collectibles, so the high end of the sweep is the realistic one.

| Tax rate | Embedded gain | Cost of NAV | Repaid in |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 15.0% | ×0.5 | 5.00% | 19.6 yrs |
| 20.0% | ×0.5 | 6.67% | 26.4 yrs |
| 23.8% | ×0.5 | 7.93% | 31.6 yrs |
| 23.8% | ×3.0 | 17.85% | 75.1 yrs |

Moving an existing, appreciated GLD position never pays. This is a rule for **new money**.

**4. The long/short version (ASSUMPTION, swept).** Long GLDM, short GLD, 2 bp one-way × NAV
on both legs, one turn a year: gross +26.17 bp/yr becomes **+18.17 bp/yr before borrow**,
and dies above roughly **18 bp/yr** of borrow — well inside what a bullion ETF actually
costs to borrow. A 26 bp spread is an ownership decision, not a trade.

## Synthetic control (machinery proof only — never supports the stamp)

- **Planted** ladder (30 bp/yr gap): the stack recovers **+30.98 bp/yr** (naive *t* = +2.55),
  Spearman **−1.000** (*p* = 0.0167), pass-through slope **−1.041** (R² 0.999).
- **Null** × 8 seeds (every wrapper charging the cohort-average fee while the published
  sheet still shows dispersion): spread mean **−0.47 bp/yr** (sd 1.07), |*t*| ≥ 2 in
  **0/8**, mean Spearman **+0.188**, *p* < 0.05 in **0/8**.

The detector fires on a planted effect and stays silent on the null, so the real-tape result
is a property of the gold-wrapper tape and not of the harness.

## Verdict

- **Signal — Real.** The cheapest-minus-priciest spread is **+26.17 bp/yr with a naive
  *t* = +3.18** (HAC +6.32, and inflated — see the bandwidth table), an **iid** bootstrap CI
  **[+9.5, +41.9]** clear of zero, 65/96 months and **9/9 calendar years** positive, positive
  in both eras (+20.98 / +30.21, significant in the late one), and — the cut that carries no
  fee assumption at all — **+26.66 with *t* = +2.69 on the fee-stable sub-window**. Across the
  cohort, ten of ten pairwise spreads carry the sign the fee sheet predicts and the fee ranking
  inverts the outcome ranking **perfectly** (Spearman −1.0000, at the 0.0167 exact-permutation
  floor, pass-through −0.89 to −0.94, R² 0.99). The mechanism is contractual, not discovered:
  a sponsor fee is deducted with certainty. Named limits: only the coarse ranking resolves —
  on the honest *t* just the widest pair clears |*t*| = 2, the two 22-bp pairs sit at 1.9 and
  the four single-digit gaps print |*t*| ≤ 0.6 against a 22.5 bp/yr floor; the early era is not
  significant on its own; the fee sheet is an ASSUMPTION carrying hindsight and the pair choice
  is a selection off it; the five wrappers are survivors.
- **Tradability — Investable.** Not because the tape pins the number down — the honest
  interval is **10 to 42 bp** — but because the act is a **purchase decision with no forecast,
  no timing, no turnover and no capacity constraint** on the wrapper that wins, and because
  even at the bottom of that interval the cheap wrapper is not the worse choice: it is a
  dominance argument, not a forecast. GLDM turns over $433m a day and repays even a 30 bp
  execution penalty inside fourteen months, and the gap compounds to **2.6% of terminal wealth
  over ten years**. Three things it is *not*: it is not a reason to sell an appreciated GLD
  position (19 to 75 years to repay the collectibles tax bill), it is not a long/short trade
  (dead above ~18 bp/yr of borrow), and it is not an argument for the fee-cheapest wrapper at
  any size — BAR's $21m/day cannot take an institutional ticket. Buy the cheap wrapper today;
  never trade it.
